source.title: Improved generalization bounds of group invariant / equivariant deep networks via quotient feature spaces
source.authors: Akiyoshi Sannai; M. Imaizumi; M. Kawano

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including supplementary proofs; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own synthetic-data experiment measuring generalization gaps for DeepSets as permutation-invariance degree changes. It tests a related condition through a different dataset and task than the listed original sources; it does not test the claim's memorization or natural-label setting.
record.gate_note: The paper also derives theoretical bounds and discusses expressive power; those are not empirical outcome rows. The experiment reports only mean gap trends in Figure 4, without numerical gap values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study derives bounds for invariant/equivariant networks and measures how DeepSets' generalization gap changes with permutation-invariance degree on synthetic sum regression. Neither its theory nor its experiment tests any of V1–V8. A different generalization question does not qualify as T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the experimental conclusion but omits the paper's main theoretical conclusions: quotient feature spaces quantify improved generalization bounds for invariant/equivariant networks, and permutation-invariant networks retain an optimal approximation rate. The experiment is presented as supporting the predicted decrease in gap with invariance degree.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic regression experiment with DeepSets; varies permutation-invariance degree rather than testing the original claim's natural-label generalization or memorization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization-gap trend changes with n, the permutation-invariance degree.

fits_no_version.finding: For DeepSets on synthetic sum regression, the authors report that the mean generalization gap decreases as n increases from 2 to 8, with N fixed at 48 and d decreasing accordingly. They report agreement between the experimental and theoretical slopes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing permutation-invariance degree can reduce the generalization gap in this synthetic regression setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI 2021)
record.problems: The empirical validation uses synthetic sum regression, one architecture and a single stated training recipe. Figure 4 is the only source of experimental gap values; the text reports a mean over five trials but no numerical values or error bars.
record.rows_left_out: None. The experiment reports four n settings; each is retained as a separate figure-only row because the text does not give numeric values.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation, and weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Using Adam and a fixed batch size does not test optimizer or batch-size effects. Approximation-rate results do not establish post-interpolation width behavior. The textual report establishes the invariance trend, but that trend bears on none of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison, nor local-connectivity test.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No sharpness or other measured network-property comparison.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: DeepSets
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization gap while varying n, the permutation-invariance degree, on synthetic sum regression.

conditions.value: mean over five trials with different random seeds

rows.measure: Generalization gap; the paper reports a mean curve and states the experimental slope matches the theoretical slope.
rows.uncertainty: Mean over five trials; no error bars stated.
rows.note: Figure 4 plots logarithm of the generalization gap, but the text gives no numerical value for this condition. This synthetic sum-regression result is outside the claim versions.
rows.check: No substantive extraction error identified. This invariance-degree condition does not measure any listed version; its numerical gap is unavailable in the supplied figure text.
